newsitem.title: CHINA: China soybean imports soar on low world prices.
newsitem.headline: China soybean imports soar on low world prices.

text.p: Low international prices and slumping domestic output have helped send Chinese soybean and soymeal imports soaring, a soybean official said on Tuesday.

Soybean imports soared to 650,000 tonnes in the first nine months of 1996, up by 336.8 percent year-on-year, customs statistics showed. Soymeal imports rocketed 30,352.4 percent to 926,900 tonnes, according to the figures.

Imports had been boosted by international prices for both soybean and soymeal that were now far below domestic prices, said an official of the soybean division of the China National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corp.
Imported soybean cost 2,800 yuan ($337) per tonne, much lower than the domestic price of 3,200 yuan per tonne, the official said.
Imported soymeal cost 2,500 yuan per tonne, compared to a domestic 2,900 yuan, allowing traders to reap huge profits, she told Reuters by telephone.
Slumping domestic production was another factor in rising imports, she said but gave no figures.
Dwindling profits had forced most Chinese crushing enterprises to stop processing soy products, pushing up soymeal imports, she said. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
